To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an active receiving switched-beam phased array antenna for 60 GHz applications.

a compact and high-performance 60-GHz phased array is realized by integrating a 4 ×4 Butler matrix, 4 × 2 GaAs single-poly-double-throw switches, and 4 GaAs low-noisem amplifiers on an 80-μm-thick organic substrate.
we have demonstrated a 60-Ghz active switched-beam antenna array on an LCP platform with a 1.1-W dc power consumption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the realization of active phased arrays on a low-loss, low-cost, low-temperature co-fired ceramic substrate.
the development of a compact 60-GHz active phased-array receiver on LCP platform with integrated Butler matrix and GaAs low noise amplifiers.
the realization of a low-cost, low-loss, low-power, and compact phased array antenna for future 60-GHz applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 60-GHZ receiving switched-beam phased array with an integrated Butler matrix on an LCP platform has been successfully designed and fabricated.
a compact, low-power, high-gain, low-noise switched-beam phased array is demonstrated on an organic LCP platform at 60 GHz.
the presented active phased array antenna is a first-of-a-kind and demonstrates the potential of using LCP for high-performance millimeter-wave phased array antennas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented active receiving switched-beam phased array demonstrates a working prototype with the potential for a low-cost and compact solution for future 60-GHz wireless communication systems.
this active phased array is a first step towards the realization of a low-power, low-cost and low-profile 60-GHz phased array receiver.
the presented 60-GHz switched-beam phased array is the first of its kind to be realized on an organic LCP substrate with an integrated Butler matrix, active amplifiers, and beamforming switches.
The main takeaway from our work is that

an active switched-beam antenna array is successfully demonstrated on an LCP platform with a high degree of compactness and integration, which is a promising solution to the design of future mm-wave and sub-THz phased array systems.
the active phased array can be integrated on a thin, low-loss, and lightweight organic LCP substrate.
